question: Can a Stockfish-supervised contrastive chess embedding, oriented after training by one global losing-to-winning direction, serve as the evaluator for a narrow exact-rule minimax search without a learned policy or separately trained scalar value head?

key_findings.claim: SOLIS turns continuous Stockfish win probabilities into a contrastive representation and then recovers a scalar ordering with a post-hoc global advantage vector.
key_findings.evidence: Five million ChessBench positions are normalized to White's perspective. Positions within delta=0.05 win probability are positives, with five positives sampled per anchor; a CLS Transformer produces L2-normalized embeddings. At inference, the normalized difference between the held-out p=1 and p=0 embedding means defines the advantage direction, and legal children are ranked by their projection on it.

anchors.section: 3.1-3.3 Input Representation, Encoder Architecture, and Supervised Contrastive Training

key_findings.claim: The two advertised scoring mechanisms are algebraically identical for every ranking and fixed-depth minimax decision described in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: The unanchored score is <z',a>, whereas the anchored score is <z'-mu_Black,a>=<z',a>-<mu_Black,a>. The second term is one state-independent constant. It therefore cannot change child order, Top-W membership, leaf ordering, min/max choices, or the selected root move. No normalization or state-dependent anchor is introduced after subtraction.

key_findings.claim: The reported stability and playing-strength differences between anchored and unanchored scoring cannot be caused by the published formulas.
key_findings.evidence: The authors report a steady 10-30 Elo Base gain from anchoring and distinct match scores, including Base depth 3 changing from 106-94 to 98-102 and Mini depth 5 from 101-99 to 113-87. Since anchoring subtracts a constant, these differences can only reflect independent match sampling, an undocumented implementation difference, or an error in the equations/results—not the stated mechanism.

key_findings.claim: The 'no value head' framing is technically narrow: SOLIS still evaluates each state with a fixed linear scalar head derived from Stockfish-labeled extremes.
key_findings.evidence: The encoder has no jointly trained value-output module, but action selection is exactly the scalar functional z -> <z,a>, with a estimated from p=1 and p=0 Stockfish-labeled states. It also enumerates exact legal moves and applies recursive White-max/Black-min search. Thus it removes a trained value-head parameterization, not scalar evaluation, search, chess rules, or expert-evaluation supervision.

key_findings.claim: The contrastive objective enforces local outcome neighborhoods, not the claimed global one-dimensional losing-to-winning order.
key_findings.evidence: Pairs inside a delta threshold are pulled together and larger-gap pairs are pushed apart, but this metric loss is invariant to rotations and does not impose monotonic projection on any axis. The global axis is fitted afterward from two extreme means. The paper gives a UMAP colored by labels but no held-out rank correlation, calibration error, pairwise ordering accuracy, residual multidimensional structure, or comparison against directly regressing win probability.

key_findings.claim: The implementation is a compact learned evaluator paired with aggressive fixed-width exact-rule search.
key_findings.evidence: Mini has six layers, width 128, eight heads, MLP 256, and 0.8M parameters; Base has six layers, width 1024, 16 heads, MLP 1024, and 41M parameters. Each node embeds legal children, retains the top W, recursively applies min-max preference to depth S, and uses Zobrist transpositions. Main equal-depth tests fix W=3 and S in {3,4,5}.

key_findings.claim: Reported capped-Stockfish ratings rise with depth and exceed 2500 at depth five, but they are estimates on an adaptively selected artificial opponent scale rather than evidence of 2500 human or unrestricted-engine strength.
key_findings.evidence: Each configuration plays 600+ games under a stated 50 ms per-move setup against Stockfish 16 with UCI_LimitStrength and selected Elo caps; caps are explicitly chosen so every configuration has both a positive- and negative-win-rate matchup. BayesElo produces 95% intervals. The paper does not test humans, Lichess, a fixed opening benchmark, raw Stockfish, or an external calibrated engine pool.

key_findings.claim: At W=3 the Base model earns more points than the configured Stockfish equal-depth opponent in five of six reported scoring/depth cells, while Mini is uneven.
key_findings.evidence: Across 200 games per cell, Base direct scores are 106, 109, and 107.5 at depths 3-5 versus 94, 91, and 92.5; Base anchored scores are 98, 108, and 110 versus 102, 92, and 90. Mini direct scores are 108, 85, and 101; anchored scores are 105, 91, and 113. No uncertainty interval or hypothesis test accompanies these 200-game totals.

key_findings.claim: Equal nominal depth is not a controlled search-compute comparison, and the broad 'far fewer nodes' conclusion fails at the deepest reported average.
key_findings.evidence: SOLIS's full W=3 trees contain at most 40, 121, and 364 nodes at depths 3, 4, and 5. Stockfish averages 137, 214, and 338 nodes, with maxima 1,625, 4,463, and 10,611. SOLIS therefore evaluates 26 more nodes than Stockfish on average at depth five. Nominal depth also ignores Stockfish quiescence, extensions, reductions, pruning semantics, transposition reuse, and the cost of a Transformer evaluation per child.

key_findings.claim: The claimed compute efficiency is not substantiated by end-to-end measurements.
key_findings.evidence: The evaluation says games use a fixed 50 ms per-move limit, but does not state SOLIS hardware, batching, achieved latency, wall-clock distribution, Transformer FLOPs, energy, transposition-hit rate, or whether all SOLIS configurations actually finish within the cap. Counting search nodes treats a neural embedding evaluation as commensurate with a Stockfish node and excludes the six-L40S training cost.

key_findings.claim: Match independence and opening diversity are not documented, leaving a serious deterministic-game confound.
key_findings.evidence: The paper states alternating colors and 200 games per equal-depth cell, but names no opening suite, randomized opening plies, seed, temperature, tie-breaking randomness, starting-position distribution, duplicate-game count, or adjudication rule. Fixed-depth deterministic engines repeatedly starting from the initial board could reproduce the same games, so 200 nominal games need not supply 200 independent observations.

key_findings.claim: The widening study supports only a local W=3 heuristic under the tested configuration, not the stronger inference that representation quality replaces broad expansion.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 3-4 test widths 1, 2, 3, and 5 and the text reports a jump at three with little gain at five. There is no matched-latency curve, uncertainty-aware width comparison, tactical-position stratification, larger width, policy-prior baseline, or exhaustive/oracle analysis showing that the correct continuation is generally among the top three.

key_findings.claim: The qualitative UMAP evidence does not establish interpretability, smoothness, or a causal planning coordinate.
key_findings.evidence: One test-set UMAP and three selected game paths are shown. UMAP can manufacture visually smooth neighborhoods, connecting temporally adjacent points makes paths look continuous, and decisive games are expected to correlate with the Stockfish labels used for training. No projection stability, path-length null, counterfactual move analysis, quantitative trajectory statistic, or human interpretability study is reported.

key_findings.claim: The representation omits repetition history and cannot rank winning lines by urgency; the appendices show both failures in play.
key_findings.evidence: FEN lacks prior-position history, allowing perpetual-check/repetition draws from otherwise winning states. All checkmates receive p=1 regardless of mate length, so mate-in-1 and mate-in-20 are indistinguishable and long continuations can invite complications. Game C ends in a repeated-position draw; Game I turns many winning continuations into a draw; Game D is presented as a weakness involving short-sighted play.

key_findings.claim: The paper overstates fifty-move-rule blindness because the declared 77-token FEN includes the half-move clock.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3.1 explicitly says FEN encodes the half-move clock, yet immediately repeats the source-paper claim that omitted past states make the fifty-move rule non-Markovian. Full move history is essential for repetition, but the half-move clock is precisely the sufficient state variable for the ordinary fifty-move counter; only implementation/rule subtleties beyond the stated representation could remain.

key_findings.claim: Dataset and split reporting is insufficient to rule out leakage or quantify generalization.
key_findings.evidence: Training runs 400,000 batches of 128, exposing roughly 51.2M anchor draws from a five-million-position corpus, but the paper gives no train/validation/test sizes, game-level split, deduplication, position-source distribution, extreme-mean sample count, label engine settings, or overlap analysis between ChessBench positions and evaluation trajectories. Delta and tau were selected experimentally, yet the selection criterion and split are unspecified.

key_findings.claim: The evaluation omits the most direct learned-chess baselines and therefore cannot isolate the value of embedding arithmetic.
key_findings.evidence: SOLIS adopts ChessBench's dataset and tokenization but does not compare against ChessBench/Chessformer evaluators, a scalar win-probability regressor with the same encoder and search, DeepChess's pairwise comparator, Giraffe, a policy-pruned neural evaluator, or an ablation using raw Stockfish win probabilities. Stockfish is the only quantitative baseline, confounding representation, evaluator architecture, search policy, implementation, and compute.

key_findings.claim: Reproducibility remains incomplete despite extensive score tables.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix supplies core training hyperparameters, Stockfish 16 settings, representative PGNs, and W-D-L counts for the capped-rating runs. It does not supply code, checkpoints, data split manifests, random seeds, opening lists, exact hardware/software for inference, training time, learning-rate schedule details, or a deterministic route from tables to figures. The pinned v1 only states that LLMs were used for minor formatting and figure/table placement.

anchors.section: A.1 Use of Large Language Models

key_findings.claim: Transfer beyond chess is speculative and rests on restrictive access assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: Only deterministic, perfect-information chess is tested, with exact legal dynamics and dense expert state evaluations supplied by Stockfish. No experiment covers learned or stochastic dynamics, partial observability, continuous control, nonstationary rewards, action costs, safety constraints, or domains in which p=0 and p=1 extreme sets are sparse or unavailable.

method.core_idea: Learn a metric embedding of chess positions from expert win probabilities, orient it with the difference between mean embeddings at the two label extremes, and use the resulting scalar projection both to prune legal children and evaluate leaves in a shallow minimax tree.
method.mechanism: A fixed-length FEN tokenizer feeds a CLS Transformer trained with supervised contrastive loss. At inference, exact chess rules enumerate children, every child is encoded, the W largest projections on a global White-advantage vector survive, and recursion maximizes for White and minimizes for Black through depth S with a Zobrist transposition table. The published anchored variant merely subtracts the constant projection of the Black mean and is decision-equivalent to the direct variant.
assumptions: Stockfish win probability is an adequate target for strategic value and its label errors below delta=0.05 are negligible.
Local outcome similarity learned by SupCon yields a globally ordered projection after orienting only with p=0 and p=1 mean embeddings.
The same global linear direction evaluates tactically and positionally diverse states, phases, material regimes, and sides to move.
Top-W ranking preserves the moves required by later minimax search, despite ranking children before deeper consequences are known.
Exact chess rules provide a free, reversible dynamics model and legal-action generator.
A FEN snapshot contains enough state for evaluation except acknowledged history-sensitive outcomes.
Capped Stockfish opponents and equal nominal depths provide meaningful comparative strength estimates.
Nominal node count is an informative compute proxy across a Transformer evaluator and Stockfish's hand-engineered search.
Evaluation games are sufficiently diverse and independent even though their opening/randomization protocol is unstated.
Held-out extreme means are representative and estimated without contamination from evaluation states.

techniques.role: Expands a complete FEN snapshot into a fixed-length Transformer input following ChessBench.
Uses Stockfish win-probability distance below 0.05 to define positive position pairs.
Maps each position to an L2-normalized 128- or 1024-dimensional latent vector.
Orients the latent space with the normalized p=1 mean minus p=0 mean.
Assigns each child a scalar White-advantage score without a separately trained prediction head.
Retains only the W children most favored by the global direction before deeper search.
Selects moves by alternating White maximization and Black minimization through S plies.
Avoids re-encoding repeated positions within search.
Fits rating and confidence intervals from matches against several UCI-limited Stockfish levels.
Provides a qualitative two-dimensional visualization of labeled states and three selected games.

evaluations.setting: Five million Stockfish-evaluated ChessBench positions; Mini and Base encoders trained for 400,000 steps on six L40S GPUs
evaluations.metric: Qualitative UMAP separation by White win probability
evaluations.result: The plotted test positions show gold and green outcome regions with intermediate colors between them, but no quantitative embedding or calibration statistic is reported
evaluations.baseline: No scalar-regression, alternative contrastive objective, random-label, or direct ChessBench evaluator baseline

evaluations.setting: 600+ games per search configuration against Stockfish 16 at several adaptively chosen UCI Elo caps under a stated 50 ms per-move limit
evaluations.result: Ratings generally rise with depth; both anchored models exceed 2500 at depth five and Base is reported 10-30 Elo stronger when anchored
evaluations.baseline: Artificially rating-capped Stockfish pool, not unrestricted Stockfish, humans, or an external engine ladder

evaluations.setting: Equal-depth W=3 Base versus Stockfish, 200 alternating-color games at depths 3, 4, and 5
evaluations.result: Direct Base scores 106/109/107.5; anchored Base scores 98/108/110 out of 200
evaluations.baseline: Stockfish at the same nominal depth with default variable expansion, scoring the complementary totals

evaluations.setting: Equal-depth W=3 Mini versus Stockfish, 200 alternating-color games at depths 3, 4, and 5
evaluations.result: Direct Mini scores 108/85/101; anchored Mini scores 105/91/113 out of 200, with a marked depth-four reversal
evaluations.baseline: Stockfish at the same nominal depth with default variable expansion

evaluations.setting: Node-count comparison for W=3 search at depths 3-5
evaluations.metric: Maximum SOLIS full-tree nodes versus Stockfish mean and maximum reported nodes per move
evaluations.result: SOLIS maxima are 40/121/364; Stockfish means are 137/214/338 and maxima 1,625/4,463/10,611, so SOLIS is below the mean only at depths three and four
evaluations.baseline: Stockfish INFO_ALL node counter; no wall-clock, FLOP, or energy comparison

evaluations.setting: Width ablation W in {1,2,3,5} across search depths
evaluations.result: The text reports a clear gain through W=3 and little further gain at W=5
evaluations.baseline: Other SOLIS widths; no matched-compute policy, scalar evaluator, or unrestricted-width baseline

evaluations.setting: Three selected real-game paths over a shared UMAP
evaluations.metric: Visual movement toward White-favored, neutral, or Black-favored regions
evaluations.result: The chosen win, draw, and loss trajectories look smooth and qualitatively align with their outcomes
evaluations.baseline: No random-game, shuffled-order, alternative-projection, quantitative path, or annotator baseline

evaluations.setting: Nine appendix PGNs spanning capped-Stockfish and equal-depth examples
evaluations.metric: Qualitative tactical success and observed errors
evaluations.result: Examples include sacrifices and conversions as well as a repetition draw, short-horizon weakness, and failure to finish among many winning continuations
evaluations.baseline: Selected case studies rather than a prespecified error taxonomy over all games

evaluations.setting: Appendix A.6 full W-D-L tables for anchored and unanchored capped-opponent configurations
evaluations.metric: Wins, draws, losses and opponent rating cap by depth/width/model
evaluations.result: Tables expose the match inputs used for rating estimation across pages 17-20
evaluations.baseline: No released scripts, openings, seeds, or independent reproduction artifact

limitations: Author-stated: snapshot FEN cannot encode prior-position history, so SOLIS is blind to threefold repetition and can concede perpetual draws.
Author-stated: equal p=1 labels make mate-in-1 indistinguishable from mate-in-20, producing indecision and avoidable draws or losses.
Author-stated: transfer beyond chess, rule-aware features, forced-win preferences, policy priors, MCTS, calibration, and uncertainty remain future work.
Reviewer-identified: the anchored method is exactly a constant shift of the direct score and cannot cause the reported behavioral differences.
Reviewer-identified: no held-out scalar-value quality, order accuracy, calibration, or uncertainty metric validates the central embedding claim.
Reviewer-identified: no matched-architecture scalar regression, ChessBench/Chessformer, DeepChess, Giraffe, policy, or AlphaZero-style baseline isolates the contribution of embedding arithmetic.
Reviewer-identified: UCI Elo caps are selected after requiring both positive and negative matchups and do not establish human, Lichess, or unrestricted-engine Elo.
Reviewer-identified: opening diversity, starting positions, engine randomness, seeds, duplicate games, adjudication, and effective sample size are omitted.
Reviewer-identified: equal nominal depth and node counts do not equalize compute or algorithmic work across the two engines.
Reviewer-identified: at depth five SOLIS's maximum fixed tree of 364 nodes exceeds Stockfish's reported average of 338, weakening the unqualified fewer-nodes claim.
Reviewer-identified: inference hardware, achieved latency, batching, FLOPs, power, and end-to-end time are absent, so lightweight/compute-efficient claims are unresolved.
Reviewer-identified: dataset splits, game-level leakage controls, deduplication, extreme-set sizes, and hyperparameter-selection protocol are absent.
Reviewer-identified: the global direction assumes one linear value axis works across all chess regimes; no phase-, tactic-, or uncertainty-stratified analysis is given.
Reviewer-identified: UMAP and three selected paths are qualitative and projection-dependent, with no causal or human interpretability test.
Reviewer-identified: the appendix gives tables and PGNs but no code, checkpoints, splits, openings, seeds, or executable reproduction pipeline.
Reviewer-identified: the fifty-move-rule claim is overbroad because the described FEN explicitly includes the half-move clock.
Reviewer-identified: deterministic perfect-information chess with exact rules and dense Stockfish labels is much easier than the proposed broader control setting.
failure_modes: Anchored and direct implementations yield different moves even though the equations are rank-equivalent, revealing an undocumented operation or implementation defect.
The global projection ranks a locally appealing child in the top three while pruning the only move whose deeper continuation is winning.
Two strategically different positions with similar Stockfish win probability collapse together under the contrastive margin despite requiring different actions.
A nonlinear or multimodal value manifold is poorly represented by the single extreme-mean direction, causing phase-specific ranking reversals.
Positions far from the p=0/p=1 training extremes receive overconfident scalar projections without calibration or uncertainty handling.
Perpetual checks or prior repetitions force a draw because identical FEN snapshots do not carry occurrence history.
Mate-length blindness chooses a longer winning line, allowing complications, a repetition, or a tactical escape.
Fixed W=3 pruning misses sacrificial or temporarily losing moves whose benefit appears beyond the shallow horizon.
A transposition entry aliases states whose legal draw status differs because repetition history is not part of the key/state.
Capped-opponent or repeated-opening evaluation inflates rating estimates relative to diverse, unrestricted play.
Transformer inference dominates runtime despite fewer nominal nodes, invalidating the intended constrained-compute advantage.
Win-probability label noise, duplicates, or train/evaluation game overlap lets the encoder memorize common positions rather than learn transferable strategic geometry.
A visually smooth UMAP path persists under a poor evaluator because the projection emphasizes label neighborhoods rather than decision quality.
The white-perspective scalar or side-to-move handling is implemented inconsistently, reversing pruning or leaf preferences for Black.
Transfer to partial observation or stochastic dynamics fails because a single observed state has no unique value and exact successor generation is unavailable.
reusable_insights: Always simplify affine scoring variants algebraically before attributing empirical gains; subtracting one global constant cannot change a ranking or minimax policy.
Separate 'no trained value head' from 'no scalar value function': a fixed latent projection remains a linear evaluation head operationally.
A metric-learning objective does not by itself identify an ordered global coordinate; evaluate the downstream axis with rank, calibration, and counterfactual tests.
Use a matched encoder plus direct scalar regression as the minimum baseline when claiming that contrastive geometry adds planning value.
Report search quality against latency/FLOP budgets, not only nominal depth or node count across radically different evaluators.
Deterministic game-engine evaluation needs a declared opening suite, seeds/tie-breaking, duplicate-game accounting, and effective sample size.
History-sensitive rules must be part of the state and transposition key, not patched only at terminal evaluation.
Outcome probability needs a secondary notion of urgency or distance-to-terminal to distinguish equally winning continuations.
Test whether top-k pruning retains oracle-best moves by tactical category and horizon before inferring that small width captures the important branches.
Visual latent trajectories should be paired with projection-robust statistics, shuffled controls, and action-level counterfactuals.
Distinguish an expert-label compression result from autonomous reinforcement learning: SOLIS amortizes Stockfish evaluations and relies on exact rules.
Treat capped-engine ratings as protocol-specific estimates and avoid translating them to human or open-pool strength without calibration.
open_questions: What undocumented implementation detail, if any, makes the published anchored and direct variants produce different results?
Does a scalar win-probability regression head on the same Mini/Base encoder outperform the global contrastive direction at equal training and inference compute?
What are held-out Spearman correlation, pairwise ordering accuracy, calibration error, and tactical-category error for the projection?
How much strength remains under a fixed, diverse opening suite with deterministic seeds and unrestricted Stockfish at genuinely matched wall-clock budgets?
Does W=3 retain the oracle-best move across quiet positions, sacrifices, defenses, endgames, and different search horizons?
How sensitive are Elo and match-point claims to independent reruns, openings, tie-breaking, adjudication, and multiple-comparison correction?
Can repetition counts, half-move status, and mate distance be added without destroying the learned geometry or transposition efficiency?
Would multiple learned directions or a nonlinear scalar probe materially improve phase-specific evaluation while retaining interpretability?
Does the contrastive encoder transfer to unseen opening families, composed studies, Chess960, or label engines other than Stockfish?
What are actual per-move latency, hardware utilization, FLOPs, energy, and total training amortization relative to Stockfish and learned evaluators?
Can a projection-robust causal intervention along the advantage direction change predicted and realized outcomes, rather than merely visualize correlation?
Which domains beyond chess provide exact dynamics, dense reliable evaluations, and meaningful outcome extremes, and how does SOLIS behave when any assumption fails?

competitive_landscape.title: Amortized Planning with Large-Scale Transformers: A Case Study on Chess
competitive_landscape.difference: Ruoss et al. introduce ChessBench and the same FEN-style tokenization, train action-value and state-value Transformers from Stockfish, and report a 270M model reaching 2895 Lichess blitz without explicit search. SOLIS is smaller and couples a contrastively learned fixed projection to shallow minimax, so novelty is not amortized chess planning itself but this particular representation-plus-pruning construction.

competitive_landscape.title: Mastering Chess with a Transformer Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Chessformer studies chess-specific positional encoding and learned Transformer evaluation with playing-strength and puzzle comparisons. It is a direct omitted baseline for whether SOLIS's contrastive projection improves evaluation or compute rather than benefiting from Transformer capacity and chess supervision generally.

competitive_landscape.title: Giraffe: Using Deep Reinforcement Learning to Play Chess
competitive_landscape.relationship: learned evaluation plus shallow search predecessor
competitive_landscape.difference: Giraffe learns a chess position evaluator and move-probability components and embeds them in alpha-beta-style search. SOLIS replaces the explicit learned scalar output with a post-hoc global projection and uses fixed-width minmax, but the broader combination of learned evaluation and selective shallow search predates it by a decade.

competitive_landscape.title: DeepChess: End-to-End Deep Neural Network for Automatic Learning in Chess
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepChess learns to compare pairs of positions and uses that preference in alpha-beta search, avoiding a conventional handcrafted scalar evaluator. It is especially close to SOLIS's relative latent-ranking motivation; SOLIS instead derives every comparison from one global linear direction learned from outcome-neighborhood embeddings.

competitive_landscape.title: Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play with a General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
competitive_landscape.difference: AlphaZero learns policy and value from self-play and combines them with MCTS, achieving unrestricted superhuman engine strength without Stockfish labels. SOLIS is much cheaper and simpler but depends on Stockfish supervision, a single global value probe, exact dynamics, fixed-width minimax, and only constrained-engine comparisons.

competitive_landscape.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
competitive_landscape.difference: MuZero learns latent dynamics, reward, policy, and value sufficient for MCTS without knowing environment rules. SOLIS does not learn dynamics and requires exact legal successor generation; its narrower novelty is using outcome-aligned embedding projection as the leaf evaluator and pruning score.

competitive_landscape.title: Latent Planning via Expansive Tree Search
competitive_landscape.difference: Gieselmann and Pokorny learn contrastive latent states, dynamics, and density and plan with an expansive latent tree/MPC on visual-control tasks. SOLIS cites this work but avoids learned dynamics by using chess rules and orients state embeddings with a global expert-outcome direction; it does not demonstrate the broader unknown-dynamics setting.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: SOLIS is a lightweight alternative to policy/value-head or learned-dynamics planning: supervised contrastive learning creates an evaluation-aligned latent chess space, one global advantage vector supports direct vector-arithmetic ranking, and W=3 shallow search reaches 2500+ capped-opponent Elo while remaining interpretable.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper provides two encoder scales, five-million-position Stockfish supervision, capped-opponent rating curves, six equal-depth match tables per model, node counts, three UMAP paths, representative PGNs, and full appendix W-D-L tables. It does not provide a quantitative latent-order test or a matched learned-evaluator baseline.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the compact combination of outcome-neighborhood contrastive training, an extreme-mean linear probe, and aggressive top-W minimax in chess. Learned chess evaluation, pairwise comparison, shallow search, amortized planning, and contrastive latent tree planning all preexist it. More importantly, the two claimed scoring variants are mathematically the same, so their central ablation is invalid as written. Evidence supports an interesting constrained-engine prototype, not the claimed anchored mechanism, general compute efficiency, 2500-equivalent open strength, or transfer beyond exact-rule expert-labeled chess. Confidence in this assessment is high because every formula and result table in the pinned v1 was checked, but no independent engine rerun or author implementation was available.

reviewer_notes: Atomic full-text review of all 20 pinned pages: abstract and Sections 1-5; equations and Figures 1-5; Tables 1-3; references; LLM-use statement; training and Stockfish setups; all nine representative PGNs on pages 13-16; and complete anchored/unanchored Elo W-D-L Tables 4-5 on pages 17-20. The cached PDF was independently fetched as official arXiv:2511.09477v1 and its SHA-256 matched the pinned artifact. The official arXiv record was checked 2026-08-23 and still exposed only v1 (submitted 2025-11-12). Seven distinct official primary-source competitors were checked at their stated exact versions. Central audit result: score_anch(z)=score_dir(z)-<mu_Black,a>, so all reported anchored/direct policy differences require undocumented behavior or sampling variance. No code, model, split, opening protocol, or independent engine reproduction was available; empirical claims are therefore reported, not revalidated.
